item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 151742
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
Issued by the NWS Weather Prediction Center College Park MD
1100 AM PDT Tue Sep 15 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Depression Fifteen-E, located well west-southwest of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula and has issued the
final advisory on former Tropical Depression Norbert.

Southwest of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form well offshore of southwestern
Mexico by the end of the week. Environmental conditions appear
conducive for some gradual development by the weekend, and this
system could become a tropical depression early next week while
it moves slowly northwestward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

Gulf of California:
A small area of low pressure has formed over the southern Gulf of
California accompanied by disorganized showers and thunderstorms.
While this system has only a slight chance of formation before it
moves inland tomorrow over the state of Sonora, periods of heavy
rain and isolated flooding are possible over that state during the
next couple of days.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...10 percent.

Western Portion of the Eastern Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form over the western portion
of the eastern Pacific this weekend. Some gradual development of
this system is possible early next week as it moves westward
at 10 to 15 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Jackson/Blake

item.title: Tropical Depression Fifteen-E Public Advisory Number 9
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Tue Sep 15 2026 
766 
WTPZ35 KNHC 152039
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Fifteen-E Advisory Number   9
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP152026
Issued by the NWS Weather Prediction Center College Park MD
200 PM PDT Tue Sep 15 2026
 
...DEPRESSION WEAKENING...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM PDT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.7N 125.0W
ABOUT 1100 MI...1775 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...30 MPH...45 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WSW OR 255 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1006 MB...29.71 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression
Fifteen-E was located near latitude 15.7 North, longitude 125.0
West. The depression is moving toward the west-southwest near 12 mph
(19 km/h) and this general motion is expected to continue through 
tomorrow or until it dissipates.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 30 mph (45 km/h) with higher gusts.
This system is forecast to dissipate within a day or so.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1006 mb (29.71 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Jackson/Blake

item.title: Tropical Depression Fifteen-E Forecast Discussion Number 8
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Tue Sep 15 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 151446
TCDEP5
 
Tropical Depression Fifteen-E Discussion Number   8
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP152026
Issued by the NWS Weather Prediction Center College Park MD
800 AM PDT Tue Sep 15 2026
 
Convection is still displaced to the southeast of the low-level
center of the depression per infrared and proxy-visible satellite 
imagery. The 0804 UTC OSCAT scatterometer pass indicated that the 
center remains elongated with maximum winds of about 30 kt. 
Therefore, the initial intensity is kept at 30 kt for this advisory.
 
The system is moving at an estimated motion of 260/10 kt. A 
generally westward motion is forecast over the next few days as the 
system is steered along the southern edge of a mid-level ridge.
The latest NHC track forecast is similar to the previous one and 
relied on the Google DeepMind and HCCA aids.
 
The depression remains within a moderate wind shear environment 
near a mid- to upper-level low, with dry mid-level air entraining 
into the center. While shear is forecast to decrease later 
today, the dry air entrainment should limit significant 
development, though it is possible the system could briefly become 
a tropical storm. Wind shear is expected to increase again in 
a couple days, causing the system to struggle to produce deep 
convection. Thus, the depression is forecast to become a 
post-tropical cyclone by 60 h, and open into a trough by day 4.  No 
large changes were made to the previous advisory.
